scr_ar_clearing_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.purpose: Clears an open A/R credit adjustment by applying it against the customer's open invoices, so the credit and the invoice net off instead of both remaining open.
scr_ar_clearing_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.outcome: Customer credits are consumed and the aging shows a true net balance.
scr_ar_clearing_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.rootCause: A credit adjustment posted but never applied leaves the invoice showing as overdue and the credit showing as owed back, which inflates both receivables and credit balances.
scr_ar_clearing_an_a_r_credit_adjustment.ifSkipped: The aging overstates what the customer owes, and collections chase a balance that has already been credited.
redFlags: Open credit adjustments older than 60 days

scr_ar_deleting_adjustments.purpose: Deletes A/R adjustments that are still drafts or were entered in error before affecting the GL; posted adjustments must be reversed instead.
scr_ar_deleting_adjustments.outcome: Erroneous draft adjustments removed without leaving false credits.
scr_ar_deleting_adjustments.rootCause: Draft adjustments left in the system can be posted by mistake later, crediting customers who were never owed anything.
scr_ar_deleting_adjustments.ifSkipped: Stale draft credits are posted accidentally and reduce revenue.

scr_ar_reversing_adjustments.purpose: Reverses a posted A/R adjustment — for example a credit issued in error — creating an offsetting entry and reinstating the customer's balance.
scr_ar_reversing_adjustments.outcome: Wrong credits or debits are undone with an audit trail.
scr_ar_reversing_adjustments.rootCause: Posted adjustments have changed revenue and the customer ledger; reversal is the only way to correct them without destroying history.
scr_ar_reversing_adjustments.ifSkipped: Incorrect credits remain, understating revenue and receivables.
redFlags: Reversals of credits approved by management without documentation

scr_ar_other_ways_to_reverse_a_transacti.purpose: Explains alternatives for reversing A/R transactions — reversing the invoice, the payment or the adjustment — depending on what went wrong.
scr_ar_other_ways_to_reverse_a_transacti.outcome: The correct reversal method is chosen for each error.
scr_ar_other_ways_to_reverse_a_transacti.rootCause: Reversing the wrong object (the invoice instead of the misapplied payment) creates new errors; understanding the options prevents that.
scr_ar_other_ways_to_reverse_a_transacti.ifSkipped: Corrections create secondary errors in customer ledgers.
redFlags: Multiple reversals on the same transaction

scr_ar_finding_draft_or_posted_transacti.purpose: Searches adjustments and other A/R transactions by state (draft or posted), customer, date or amount from the adjustments area.
scr_ar_finding_draft_or_posted_transacti.outcome: Draft adjustments awaiting posting or review are found quickly.
scr_ar_finding_draft_or_posted_transacti.rootCause: Drafts left unposted at month-end mean approved credits are missing from the books; searching by state surfaces them.
scr_ar_finding_draft_or_posted_transacti.ifSkipped: Approved credits are never posted and customers dispute balances.
redFlags: Drafts older than the current period

scr_ar_turning_on_the_deletion_warning.purpose: Turns on a confirmation warning that appears before a user deletes an A/R transaction such as a draft invoice or adjustment, adding a checkpoint against accidental deletion.
scr_ar_turning_on_the_deletion_warning.rootCause: One-click deletion of drafts can remove the wrong record; a warning adds a checkpoint before data is lost.
scr_ar_turning_on_the_deletion_warning.ifSkipped: Transactions are deleted by accident and must be re-entered.

scr_ar_printing_an_adjustment.purpose: Prints an A/R adjustment record — customer, amount, reason and approval — for the customer file or approval evidence.
scr_ar_printing_an_adjustment.outcome: A printed record supporting the credit or debit.
scr_ar_printing_an_adjustment.rootCause: Credits to customers need documented approval; printing supports the file and audit review of credits.
scr_ar_printing_an_adjustment.ifSkipped: Approval evidence for credits is missing at audit.

scr_ar_a_r_adjustment_page.purpose: The A/R adjustment page showing the key adjustment information — customer, type, date, amount, reason and GL lines.
scr_ar_a_r_adjustment_page.outcome: A complete record for entering or reviewing an adjustment.
scr_ar_a_r_adjustment_page.rootCause: Reviewers need the reason and offset account alongside the amount to judge whether a credit was appropriate.
scr_ar_a_r_adjustment_page.ifSkipped: Adjustments are reviewed without their reasons and offsets.

scr_ar_saving_an_a_r_transaction_as_a_dr.purpose: Saves an A/R transaction (adjustment or invoice) as a draft so it can be completed or approved before posting.
scr_ar_saving_an_a_r_transaction_as_a_dr.outcome: Transactions are held without GL impact until reviewed.
scr_ar_saving_an_a_r_transaction_as_a_dr.rootCause: Credits and unusual charges often need approval; drafting separates preparation from posting.
scr_ar_saving_an_a_r_transaction_as_a_dr.ifSkipped: Unapproved customer credits post immediately and reduce revenue without review.

scr_ar_posting_an_a_r_adjustment.purpose: Posts a draft A/R adjustment (Post or Post & New), updating the customer's balance and the GL.
scr_ar_posting_an_a_r_adjustment.outcome: The approved credit or debit takes effect.
scr_ar_posting_an_a_r_adjustment.rootCause: Adjustments only change balances once posted; approved credits left in draft mean customers are still billed amounts they were told were forgiven.
scr_ar_posting_an_a_r_adjustment.ifSkipped: Approved credits never reach the customer's balance.

scr_ar_duplicating_an_a_r_adjustment.purpose: Creates a new A/R adjustment by copying an existing one — for example a recurring monthly concession agreed in a lease amendment.
scr_ar_duplicating_an_a_r_adjustment.outcome: Similar adjustments created quickly with consistent coding.
scr_ar_duplicating_an_a_r_adjustment.rootCause: Recurring concessions need identical coding each month; copying keeps them consistent.
redFlags: Copies continuing after the concession period ended

scr_ar_printing_a_transaction.purpose: Prints an A/R transaction after creation for the file or to send to the customer.
scr_ar_printing_a_transaction.outcome: A printed copy of the transaction.
scr_ar_printing_a_transaction.rootCause: Customers and auditors sometimes require paper or PDF evidence of specific transactions.
scr_ar_printing_a_transaction.ifSkipped: Transaction evidence must be recreated when requested.
redFlags: Printed copies sent to customers before posting

scr_ar_how_to_refund_a_credit_memo.purpose: Explains refunding a customer who holds a credit memo and prefers cash back rather than a credit against future invoices.
scr_ar_how_to_refund_a_credit_memo.outcome: Customer credits returned as cash and cleared from the ledger.
scr_ar_how_to_refund_a_credit_memo.rootCause: Customers leaving a property or ending a contract are owed their credits back; unrefunded credits become unclaimed property after the dormancy period.
scr_ar_how_to_refund_a_credit_memo.ifSkipped: Credits linger and become escheat obligations.

scr_ar_applying_credit_to_an_invoice.purpose: Applies a customer's available credit to an open invoice from the Receive a Payment page.
scr_ar_applying_credit_to_an_invoice.outcome: The customer's credit and open invoice net off in the ledger.
scr_ar_applying_credit_to_an_invoice.rootCause: An unapplied credit leaves the invoice looking overdue and the credit looking owed back; applying it is what makes the aging show the customer's true net position for collections.
scr_ar_applying_credit_to_an_invoice.ifSkipped: Both the credit and invoice stay open and the aging is overstated.
redFlags: Credits applied to disputed invoices without agreement

scr_ar_selecting_invoices.purpose: Filters and selects customer invoices to apply a payment or credit to on the Receive a Payment page.
scr_ar_selecting_invoices.outcome: The right invoices are chosen quickly for application.
scr_ar_selecting_invoices.rootCause: Customers with many open invoices need fast filtering so payments are applied exactly as remitted.
scr_ar_selecting_invoices.ifSkipped: Payments are applied to the wrong invoices.

scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.purpose: Applies existing customer credits to invoices without entering a new receipt, from the Enter Payments area.
scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.outcome: Credits consumed against invoices with no cash movement.
scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.rootCause: Many credit applications involve no new money; this path clears both items without a fake receipt.
scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.ifSkipped: Users create zero-dollar receipts or leave items open.
redFlags: Zero-dollar receipts used to apply credits

scr_ar_applying_credits_along_with_recor.purpose: Applies customer credits together with a new payment so both settle the selected invoices at once.
scr_ar_applying_credits_along_with_recor.outcome: Short payments from customers who deducted credits are fully reconciled.
scr_ar_applying_credits_along_with_recor.rootCause: Customers frequently pay the invoice total minus their credit; applying both together matches their remittance.
scr_ar_applying_credits_along_with_recor.ifSkipped: Invoices remain partially open despite the customer having paid in full after credits.
redFlags: Credits applied without customer remittance support

scr_ar_refunding_a_customer.purpose: Refunds a customer who has a negative balance (credit) — typically after an overpayment or a billing correction — by issuing payment through A/P.
scr_ar_refunding_a_customer.outcome: The customer is repaid and the credit cleared.
scr_ar_refunding_a_customer.rootCause: A negative balance is money owed to the customer; holding it indefinitely is both a customer-relations problem and an unclaimed property exposure.
scr_ar_refunding_a_customer.ifSkipped: Credits age into escheatable balances and customers complain.
redFlags: Refunds paid to parties other than the customer

scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.purpose: Changes the amount of a credit applied to an invoice after application, where configuration permits.
scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.outcome: Credit application errors corrected without reversing payments.
scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.rootCause: Over- or under-applying a credit is a common keying error; correcting the application directly is cleaner than reversing and redoing.
scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.ifSkipped: Errors persist or payments are unnecessarily reversed.
redFlags: Repeated changes on the same customer

scr_ar_subledgers.purpose: Chapter on the A/R subledger — opening and closing the A/R books by period and working with summaries (groups of transactions that post to the GL together).
scr_ar_subledgers.outcome: Users understand how A/R activity reaches the GL and how periods are locked.
scr_ar_subledgers.rootCause: The A/R subledger posts to the GL through summaries; controlling which summaries are open is how accounting prevents late transactions from changing reported receivables.
scr_ar_subledgers.ifSkipped: Late A/R activity posts into reported periods.
redFlags: A/R periods left open after reporting

scr_ar_subledgers_2.purpose: Explains summaries — collections of the same type of A/R transactions (invoices, payments, adjustments) grouped by period that post to the GL together.
scr_ar_subledgers_2.outcome: A/R postings organized by period and type.
scr_ar_subledgers_2.rootCause: Grouping transactions into period summaries allows whole periods to be closed and gives a clear trail from subledger to GL.

scr_ar_about_a_r_summaries.purpose: Describes A/R summaries in more detail — how they are created (automatically or manually), what they contain and how they relate to GL posting.
scr_ar_about_a_r_summaries.outcome: Users can trace A/R transactions to their GL summary.
scr_ar_about_a_r_summaries.rootCause: When A/R and GL differ, the investigation goes summary by summary; understanding them is prerequisite.
scr_ar_about_a_r_summaries.ifSkipped: Subledger-to-GL differences are hard to investigate.

scr_ar_importing_summaries.purpose: Imports A/R summaries — typically when migrating historical activity or loading opening balances.
scr_ar_importing_summaries.outcome: Historical or opening activity grouped into proper summaries.
scr_ar_importing_summaries.rootCause: Migrations need imported transactions assigned to the right period summaries for the GL to reflect them correctly.
scr_ar_importing_summaries.ifSkipped: Imported activity posts to wrong periods.

scr_ar_opening_and_closing_summaries.purpose: Explains opening and closing A/R summaries — closing prevents further posting to a period; opening allows it again.
scr_ar_opening_and_closing_summaries.rootCause: Closing summaries at month-end is how A/R cutoff is enforced; reopening must be exceptional and controlled.
scr_ar_opening_and_closing_summaries.ifSkipped: A/R cutoff is not enforced and reported receivables change.

scr_ar_closing_a_r_summaries.purpose: Closes A/R summaries for a period from Month End > Close Subledger so no further invoices, payments or adjustments post to it.
scr_ar_closing_a_r_summaries.outcome: A/R for the period is locked before the GL close.
scr_ar_closing_a_r_summaries.rootCause: Closing A/R before the GL ensures the receivable balance reported to owners cannot be changed by late activity.
scr_ar_closing_a_r_summaries.ifSkipped: Late A/R activity changes reported receivables.

scr_ar_closing_a_r_summaries_2.purpose: Procedure for closing A/R summaries either by period (all summaries for the month) or by summary name (one specific summary), from Month End > Close Subledger.
scr_ar_closing_a_r_summaries_2.rootCause: Closing by period guarantees every invoice, payment and adjustment summary for the month is locked together; closing individually risks leaving one summary open to late postings.
scr_ar_closing_a_r_summaries_2.ifSkipped: Some summaries stay open and receive late postings.

scr_ar_opening_a_r_summaries.purpose: Opens A/R summaries through Month End > Open Subledger, allowing postings again to a closed period.
scr_ar_opening_a_r_summaries.outcome: A controlled window to correct A/R in a closed period.
scr_ar_opening_a_r_summaries.rootCause: Material A/R corrections sometimes must be posted in the original period; reopening allows it but changes reported numbers.
scr_ar_opening_a_r_summaries.ifSkipped: Corrections are forced into later periods; uncontrolled reopening changes reported receivables.

scr_ar_open_the_a_r_subledger_page.purpose: The Open A/R Subledger page, restricted by permission, used to reopen a closed A/R period or specific summaries for an approved correction.
scr_ar_open_the_a_r_subledger_page.rootCause: Reopening is high-risk; a dedicated page restricted by permissions limits who can change closed periods.
scr_ar_open_the_a_r_subledger_page.ifSkipped: Closed A/R periods are reopened casually and reported receivables change.

scr_ar_opening_the_a_r_subledger.purpose: Procedure for reopening the A/R subledger for a closed period — selecting the period or summaries, documenting the reason, and re-closing after the correction posts.
scr_ar_opening_the_a_r_subledger.outcome: The period accepts A/R postings again.
scr_ar_opening_the_a_r_subledger.rootCause: Reopening must follow a defined procedure with approval because it can change reported receivables.
redFlags: Periods left open after the correction

scr_ar_finding_which_periods_are_closed.purpose: Checks which periods are closed in the books (General Ledger > Books > Close) before posting A/R activity.
scr_ar_finding_which_periods_are_closed.outcome: Users know which dates are available for posting.
scr_ar_finding_which_periods_are_closed.rootCause: Attempting to post into closed periods fails; knowing the status avoids wasted effort and backdating attempts.
scr_ar_finding_which_periods_are_closed.ifSkipped: Users try to post into closed periods or request unnecessary reopenings.

scr_ar_reopening_the_a_r_books.purpose: Reopens the books in General Ledger for a period so A/R corrections can post — a permission typically restricted to accounting managers.
scr_ar_reopening_the_a_r_books.outcome: Books reopened for an approved correction.
scr_ar_reopening_the_a_r_books.rootCause: Reopening books changes the ability to post in every application; restricted permissions ensure only authorized, documented corrections.
scr_ar_reopening_the_a_r_books.ifSkipped: Material corrections cannot be made in the right period; uncontrolled reopening changes reported results.

scr_ar_summaries_list.purpose: Lists A/R summaries (invoice, payment and adjustment groupings by period) with their status and totals, used at month-end to confirm the period's summaries are complete and closed.
scr_ar_summaries_list.outcome: Visibility of which A/R periods and summaries are open.
scr_ar_summaries_list.rootCause: Before closing the month, accounting confirms all A/R summaries for the period are closed and totals agree with the GL.
scr_ar_summaries_list.ifSkipped: Open summaries in closed periods go unnoticed.

scr_ar_viewing_the_summaries_list.purpose: Opens and filters the A/R summaries list by period, transaction type or status to review a month's summaries before closing A/R.
scr_ar_viewing_the_summaries_list.outcome: Summaries for the close are found quickly.
scr_ar_viewing_the_summaries_list.rootCause: Month-end requires reviewing all A/R summaries for the period to confirm they are complete and closed.
scr_ar_viewing_the_summaries_list.ifSkipped: Some summaries for the month are missed and stay open after close.

scr_ar_adding_a_summary.purpose: Manually adds an A/R summary for a period and transaction type, when automatic summaries are not used.
scr_ar_adding_a_summary.outcome: A container for posting a period's transactions.
scr_ar_adding_a_summary.rootCause: Without automatic summaries, a summary must exist for each period and type before transactions can post.
scr_ar_adding_a_summary.ifSkipped: Transactions cannot post or are grouped incorrectly.

scr_ar_viewing_information_about_a_summa.purpose: Views one A/R summary's details — period, type, status, totals and transactions — typically while investigating a difference between the A/R subledger and the GL.
scr_ar_viewing_information_about_a_summa.outcome: Understanding of what a summary contains and its GL impact.
scr_ar_viewing_information_about_a_summa.rootCause: Investigating A/R-to-GL differences requires opening summaries to see their transactions and totals.
scr_ar_viewing_information_about_a_summa.ifSkipped: Subledger-to-GL differences cannot be traced to specific transactions.
redFlags: Summary totals not equal to GL postings

scr_ar_editing_a_summarys_details.purpose: Edits an open A/R summary's name, date or settings — for example correcting a summary dated in the next month before any more transactions are added.
scr_ar_editing_a_summarys_details.rootCause: A summary dated in the wrong period posts all its transactions to that period; correcting it before closing avoids misstatement.
scr_ar_editing_a_summarys_details.ifSkipped: A whole summary posts to the wrong period.
redFlags: Summary date changes after transactions posted

scr_ar_deleting_summaries.purpose: Deletes empty or duplicate A/R summaries so that month-end reviews only show summaries that actually hold transactions.
scr_ar_deleting_summaries.outcome: Unused summaries removed from the list.
scr_ar_deleting_summaries.rootCause: Empty or duplicate summaries confuse close reviews and can capture postings by mistake.
scr_ar_deleting_summaries.ifSkipped: Stray summaries collect transactions in wrong periods.

scr_ar_deactivating_or_closing_a_summary.purpose: Deactivates or closes a specific A/R summary so it no longer accepts transactions.
scr_ar_deactivating_or_closing_a_summary.rootCause: Closing individual summaries allows finer control — for example locking invoices while payments for the period are still being posted.
scr_ar_deactivating_or_closing_a_summary.ifSkipped: Summaries remain open longer than intended.

scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries.purpose: Configures A/R to create summaries automatically (recommended) so each period and transaction type gets its summary without manual setup.
scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries.outcome: Consistent period grouping of A/R transactions.
scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries.rootCause: Manual summaries are error-prone (wrong dates, missing types); automatic creation removes that risk.
scr_ar_creating_automatic_summaries.ifSkipped: Manual summary errors misplace transactions in periods.

scr_ar_summary_information_page.purpose: The A/R summary record page showing its name, period, transaction type, status and totals, used as evidence that a period's A/R activity is complete and locked.
scr_ar_summary_information_page.outcome: A complete view of one A/R summary.
scr_ar_summary_information_page.rootCause: Summary status and totals are the evidence that a period's A/R activity is complete and locked.
scr_ar_summary_information_page.ifSkipped: Close evidence for the A/R period is incomplete.

scr_ar_transactions_list_of_a_summary.purpose: Lists every transaction inside an A/R summary — invoices, payments or adjustments — making up the total that posted to the GL.
scr_ar_transactions_list_of_a_summary.rootCause: Tracing a GL posting back to individual A/R transactions requires the summary's transaction list.
scr_ar_transactions_list_of_a_summary.ifSkipped: GL postings cannot be traced to transactions.
redFlags: Transactions dated outside the summary period

scr_ar_adding_transactions_to_a_summary.purpose: Adds A/R transactions to an open summary so they post to the GL in that summary's period.
scr_ar_adding_transactions_to_a_summary.outcome: Transactions grouped into the correct period summary.
scr_ar_adding_transactions_to_a_summary.rootCause: Transactions must belong to a summary to post; adding them to the right one places them in the correct period.
scr_ar_adding_transactions_to_a_summary.ifSkipped: Transactions sit unposted or in the wrong period.

scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_transactions_.purpose: Views the transactions contained in a summary to confirm completeness before closing.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_transactions_.outcome: Confidence that the summary contains exactly the period's activity.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_transactions_.rootCause: Reviewing a summary's contents before closing is the last chance to catch transactions dated in the wrong month; once closed, they can only be corrected by reversals in a later period.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_transactions_.ifSkipped: Misdated transactions are locked into the wrong period.

scr_ar_importing_transactions_into_a_sum.purpose: Imports A/R transactions from a file directly into a chosen summary, placing bulk billings or migrated history into the intended period.
scr_ar_importing_transactions_into_a_sum.outcome: Bulk transactions loaded into the correct period summary.
scr_ar_importing_transactions_into_a_sum.rootCause: Migrations and bulk billings need to land in specific period summaries; importing targets them directly.
scr_ar_importing_transactions_into_a_sum.ifSkipped: Bulk transactions land in default summaries and wrong periods.

scr_ar_editing_the_transactions_in_a_sum.purpose: Edits transactions inside an open A/R summary — correcting dates, references or coding — before the summary is closed for the period.
scr_ar_editing_the_transactions_in_a_sum.outcome: Transaction errors corrected before the summary closes.
scr_ar_editing_the_transactions_in_a_sum.rootCause: Once closed, corrections require reversals in later periods; editing while open keeps corrections in the right period.
scr_ar_editing_the_transactions_in_a_sum.ifSkipped: Errors are locked into closed summaries.
